articles.title: Rochdale foster carers recognised for supporting over 1,000 children
articles.excerpt: At an awards ceremony in Rochdale Town Hall, 34 foster families were honoured for their commitment to caring for vulnerable children, collectively fostering for 465 years.
articles.content_html:
Thirty-four foster families were honoured at the annual Foster Carer Celebration Awards held at Rochdale Town Hall, recognising their dedication to providing safe and nurturing homes for vulnerable children.

Collectively, these families have fostered for an impressive 465 years, supporting over 1,020 children and young people from newborns to 18 years old.

Among those celebrated were Michael and Marilyn, a couple from Milnrow, who have fostered for 50 years since 1976. They have cared for over 330 children, primarily focusing on newborns and siblings. Marilyn expressed her love for fostering, stating, "How long is a piece of string?" when asked how long they would continue. She reflected on the joy of seeing children grow up and receiving letters from adoptive parents thanking them for their influence.

The event highlighted the vital role foster families play in the community, providing stability and care to those in need. The awards serve not only to recognise the individual contributions of these families but also to raise awareness about the importance of fostering in Rochdale.

This recognition is significant as it underscores the ongoing need for foster carers in the area. With many children still in need of stable homes, the event aims to inspire others in the community to consider fostering.

For those interested in becoming foster carers, further information can be obtained from the local authority's fostering service.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Dedicated foster carers have looked after more than 1,000 children - Rochdale Times Skip to content LATEST NEWS Dedicated foster carers have looked after more than 1,000 children Foster carers who have between them clocked up a total of 465 years supporting children and young people across the borough have been recognised by Rochdale Council. A total of 34 fostering families were honoured at the council’s recent annual Foster Carer Celebration Awards at Rochdale Town Hall in gratitude for their outstanding commitment to providing safe, stable and nurturing homes for some of the most vulnerable. Between all the carers, it is estimated they have supported more than 1,020 children and young people from newborn to 18, while working with the local authority. Among those celebrating their individual milestones was Michael, aged 79, and Marilyn, aged 75, who are marking 50 years. Predominantly caring for newborn babies and siblings since 1976, the married couple from Milnrow have cared for more than 330 children in that time and are still welcoming youngsters into their home. Marilyn said: “We’ve been to their weddings, adoption parties, christenings, 18th and 21st birthday parties. “It’s lovely when you think you started off with them as a baby and now, they’ve grown. Ian and Carole McLean celebrate 40 years of fostering with Rochdale Council “We’ve had letters from adoptive parents saying, ‘They’ve turned out like they have because of you’ which is nice.” Michael added: “We feel privileged and proud.” Another couple who have dedicated their lives to providing a safe and stable home to those who need it the most, is Carole, 65, and Ian 67. McLean from Rochdale, who are celebrating 40 years. Ian said: “When the children do go, they always take something with them of us because we give them that stability, assistance and support. “We even give them support when they’ve gone and we’ve got a number of former foster children that we class as family and they call us mum and dad, I’ve even given two of them away at their weddings.” READ MORE: New college building reaches construction milestone Among many more memorable moments they have shared as foster carers, Carole was also the birthing partner to another former foster child, an experience she simply described as being ‘brilliant’ to be a part of. In the four decades they have provided care, they have supported more than 200 children in total. Other special milestones celebrated during the event included Richard and Susan Shaw, who are retiring as foster carers after 25 years. Speaking after the recent celebration event, Cllr Rachel Massey, cabinet member for children’s services and education, said: “Our foster carers make an extraordinary difference to the lives of children and young people across our borough every single day and thank you simply isn’t a big enough expression for how grateful we are to them. Richard and Susan Shaw retire from fostering with Rochdale Council after 25 years “The dedication, compassion and commitment shown by these families is truly inspiring, and these awards are an opportunity to recognise and celebrate everything they do. “Whether they have been fostering for a few years or several decades, each and every one of them has helped provide the stability, care and support that children need to thrive. “On behalf of Rochdale Council, I would like to thank all our foster carers for the life-changing contribution they make to our communities.” Anyone over the age of 21 with a spare room in their home can become a foster carer and support those most in need. To accommodate various lifestyles and commitments, Rochdale Council, as part of Foster for Greater Manchester, also offers a number of different fostering arrangements from respite care to long-term fostering. People with the determination to make a positive impact in a young person’s life and who would like to find out more about fostering with Rochdale Borough Council, can visit the Foster for Greater Manchester website or call 0300 303 0321. articles.content_html:
Foster carers in Milnrow were recently honoured for their remarkable collective service of 465 years at an awards ceremony held by Rochdale Borough Council. The event celebrated the commitment and dedication of these individuals who have provided care and support to children in need.

Among those recognised were Michael and Marilyn, who have fostered children for an impressive 50 years. Their long-standing service has made a significant impact on the lives of many children, and they have attended numerous events celebrating the achievements of those they have fostered.

Marilyn expressed her desire to continue fostering, highlighting the joy and fulfilment it brings to their lives.

The ceremony included heartfelt letters from adoptive parents, expressing gratitude for the care and support provided by the foster carers.

These testimonials underscored the vital role that foster carers play in the community and the positive influence they have on the lives of children and families.

This recognition not only honours the individual foster carers but also raises awareness about the importance of fostering in Rochdale.

The council encourages anyone interested in becoming a foster carer to reach out and learn more about the process, as there is always a need for dedicated individuals to provide loving homes for children.

articles.title: Traffic congestion on M62 near Rochdale following accident
articles.excerpt: An accident on the M62 has caused significant traffic delays on the eastbound carriageway between junctions 21 and 22, affecting commuters and local drivers.
articles.content_html:
Traffic congestion is building on the M62 this afternoon, October 25, following an accident on the motorway near Rochdale. The incident has resulted in partial blockage of the eastbound carriageway between junctions 21 (Milnrow) and 22 (Rishworth Moor).

According to traffic monitoring service Inrix, long queues have formed as a result of the accident, with motorists advised to expect delays. Motorway cameras show significant congestion in the area, impacting both local drivers and those travelling further afield.

Inrix later updated their report, indicating that the blockage is now attributed to a 'traffic problem' rather than a continuing accident. However, congestion remains on the eastbound carriageway, suggesting that the aftermath of the incident is still affecting traffic flow.

Motorists are encouraged to check current traffic conditions before travelling and to consider alternative routes if possible. The situation highlights the importance of staying informed about road conditions, especially during peak travel times.

articles.title: Road closures in Milnrow for Remembrance Sunday on 8 November 2026
articles.excerpt: Milnrow will see temporary road closures on 8 November 2026 for Remembrance Sunday, as announced by Rochdale Borough Council.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that several roads in Milnrow will be temporarily closed on 8 November 2026 to facilitate Remembrance Sunday events. The closures are necessary to ensure the safety of participants and attendees during the commemorative activities.

The specific roads affected by the closures have not been detailed in the announcement, but the council has indicated that alternative routes will not be provided due to the nature and duration of the event.

Local residents and visitors should plan their journeys accordingly, as access to certain areas may be restricted during the event. The council encourages everyone to be mindful of the road closures and to allow extra time for travel in the area.

For further information, including a map of the roadworks and any additional restrictions, residents can visit the Rochdale Borough Council website.

articles.title: Roadworks on Elizabethan Way in Milnrow to begin on 23 October 2026
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks will commence on Elizabethan Way in Milnrow from 9pm on Friday, 23 October 2026, until 6am on Saturday, 24 October 2026, or until the work is completed, whichever is sooner.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks will commence on Elizabethan Way in Milnrow from 9pm on Friday, 23 October 2026, until 6am on Saturday, 24 October 2026, or until the work is completed, whichever is sooner.

The roadworks will result in the temporary closure of part of Elizabethan Way, specifically between the roundabout junction and Newhey Road, covering a distance of approximately 418 metres. This closure will affect traffic in both directions, impacting local drivers and residents.

In addition to Elizabethan Way, nearby roads including Bridge Street, Dale Street, and Newhey Road may also experience disruptions during this period. Local residents and commuters are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and seek alternative routes where possible.

For further information and updates on the roadworks, residents can visit the Rochdale Borough Council website, where a map of the affected area is available.

articles.title: Cozy Market in Milnrow shut down again for selling illicit tobacco
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Trading Standards has secured a three-month closure order for Cozy Market on Dale Street, Milnrow, following repeated violations involving the sale of illegal tobacco products.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Trading Standards has successfully obtained a closure order for Cozy Market, located at 79 Dale Street, Milnrow, due to the persistent sale of illicit tobacco products. The order was granted by Manchester Magistrates' Court and will see the shop closed for three months, marking the second time it has faced such action in recent months.

The latest closure comes just weeks after the shop reopened following a previous three-month closure order issued in June. During that period, evidence of illegal tobacco sales was secured by trading standards officers, prompting the court's decision to shut the establishment again.

Rochdale Council announced the closure on its Facebook page, reiterating its commitment to tackling the sale of illegal goods in the area. The law currently allows for a three-month closure for shops found selling illicit products, but there are plans to extend this period to a year, which could further deter such activities.

The repeated closures of Cozy Market highlight ongoing issues with illegal tobacco sales in the region. Local residents and businesses may notice a reduction in illicit goods being sold, contributing to a safer shopping environment.

The council's trading standards team continues to monitor the situation closely.

articles.title: Wildhouse Meadows’ 47 homes show the gap between housing supply and low-cost housing
articles.excerpt: Lancet Homes markets Wildhouse Meadows as a 47-home development in Milnrow. Its current sales page lists three-, four- and five-bedroom houses, with advertised prices from £376,950 and selected larger homes priced substantially higher.
articles.content_html:
Lancet Homes markets Wildhouse Meadows as a 47-home development in Milnrow. Its current sales page lists three-, four- and five-bedroom houses, with advertised prices from £376,950 and selected larger homes priced substantially higher.

Those are asking prices seen during this review, not completed sale values or permanent prices. Deposit contributions are sales incentives; they do not make a property planning-defined affordable housing. A complete cost assessment also needs estate charges and the specification of the individual plot.

Lancet describes proximity to schools, the motorway and public transport. Nearby facilities are relevant, but a list of schools does not establish available places, and access to a motorway does not establish acceptable local traffic impacts.

Approval reporting identifies the former Soccer Village complex, including artificial pitches and buildings. The existence of buildings does not automatically make every recreational parcel brownfield; the precise planning boundary and current Green Belt position remain unverified.

No verified site-specific adverse legal finding against Lancet was established in this review. Customer-review allegations have not been treated as court findings.

The homes can expand choice for purchasers, but the advertised market offer cannot be counted as low-cost rented provision. For future supply, the 47-home scheme total must be reduced by homes already completed.

Location: Wildhouse Lane, Milnrow

Planning stage: Homes actively marketed; construction/completion position varies by plot

Homes: 47 scheme homes

Let or for sale: Market sale advertised; secured affordable provision not established

Land: Former Soccer Village sports complex; exact brownfield extent and Green Belt boundary unverified

Final planning agreement: The executed Section 106 deed, complete schedules, payment triggers and later variations were not verified. This is an evidence gap, not a claim that no agreement exists.

Exact rents / prices: Lancet’s page advertises market homes from £376,950; examples include Hamilton home 2 at £684,950 and Cheltenham home 27 at £789,950. Actual transaction prices and estate charges are not established; no exact affordable rent/price schedule verified.

Affordable breakdown: 47 market homes advertised. No signed affordable count verified. A separate report’s 15 Onward affordable homes relate to Stubley Meadows, not this development; they must not be transferred into this total.

Funded school capacity: No scheme-specific funded additional school places, named capital project and opening date were established from the accessible official records reviewed.

Funded healthcare capacity: No site-specific funded NHS expansion, additional staffed appointment capacity or delivery date was established from the accessible council/government records reviewed. Proximity to a surgery is not a capacity assessment.

Funded transport capacity: No complete scheme-specific transport funding schedule or evidence of delivered service capacity was established from the accessible official records reviewed. Highway conditions and marketing descriptions do not establish funded bus or rail services.

The outstanding details identified above are not yet available to Rochdale Daily. This article will be updated when the information becomes available.

Research checked 14 October 2026. Advertised prices are snapshots, not achieved sale prices.

Read the borough-wide housing investigation and the other developments: https://rochdaledaily.co.uk/articles/rochdale-housing-developments-affordability-schools-gp-transport

articles.title: Rochdale pupils learn about online safety at Milnrow Crucial Crew
articles.excerpt: Year 6 pupils from schools across the Rochdale area have taken part in police-led talks about social media safety and cyberbullying at Milnrow Cricket Club.
articles.content_html:
Year 6 pupils from schools across the Rochdale area have taken part in police-led talks about social media safety and cyberbullying at Milnrow Cricket Club.

PC Hunt, collar number 10683, and PC Eyre, collar number 10811, attended the club last week as part of the annual Crucial Crew event, according to an update supplied by PCSO Tyler Davies.

The officers discussed how children can stay safe on social media and the risks they may encounter online. The sessions also explored cyberbullying, who it can affect and the impact it can have on those targeted.

Pupils were told about ways to help prevent cyberbullying and what to do if they witnessed it, giving them an opportunity to consider how their actions online can affect other people.

PCSO Davies reported that the children were fully engaged and participated throughout the sessions. The police update thanked the pupils for their involvement.

The visit brought pupils from schools around Rochdale together at the Milnrow venue for practical discussions about staying safe online.

What helps your family talk about online safety? Share your experiences in the comments, without naming children or identifying anyone involved in a bullying incident.

articles.title: Milnrow woman's appeal against Animal ban rejected by Court
articles.excerpt: A Milnrow woman has had her appeal against a five-year ban on keeping animals dismissed by a judge after her dog was put down due to untreated injuries.
articles.content_html:
A woman from Milnrow has had her appeal against a five-year ban on keeping animals rejected by a judge at Manchester Crown Court. Anne Marie Wood was previously sentenced for causing unnecessary suffering to her dog, Tilly, who had to be euthanised after suffering from a broken leg that went untreated.

The RSPCA received a tip-off in December 2024 regarding Tilly's condition and found the Bichon Frise visibly lame and hesitant to put weight on her front leg. Wood initially refused to cooperate with inspectors but eventually allowed them into her home.

She claimed the injury occurred when Tilly fell while being passed through a front window and stated that she could not afford the necessary veterinary treatment, which was estimated to be between £400 and £500.

Despite the RSPCA's offer to take Tilly to their Greater Manchester Animal Hospital for examination, Wood declined. When Tilly was eventually seen by a vet, it was determined that her injuries were severe and that treatment could not restore an acceptable quality of life.

The decision was made to put her to sleep to prevent further suffering.

Wood, of St James Street, pleaded guilty at Tameside Magistrates Court on July 31 and received an 18-month prison sentence, suspended for one year, along with a ten-day Rehabilitation Activity Requirement and a nine-month drug rehabilitation programme.

Following the rejection of her appeal on September 30, Wood remains banned from keeping animals for five years.

articles.title: Milnrow's John Milne Table Table to close on September 3
articles.excerpt: John Milne Table Table in Milnrow will close on 3 September, with the restaurant thanking generations of customers for their support and inviting guests to visit once more.
articles.content_html:
John Milne Table Table in Milnrow will officially close its doors on Thursday, 3 September, as Table Table prepares to close its locations.

In a farewell message to guests, the restaurant said it had been an honour to serve communities across the UK, from quick mid-week dinners to decades of family celebrations.

The team thanked customers who had made the restaurant feel like home and said it hoped local diners would be able to visit at least once more and create more memories before the doors close.

The message ended simply: "Thank you for everything."

articles.title: Rainbow Health Group invites residents to open day at new clinic after 17 years on Hornby Street
articles.excerpt: The health and wellbeing clinic is moving to a new home after 17 years, and is welcoming the community to an open day this Saturday - with the Mayor and Mayoress performing the official opening at 1pm.
articles.content_html:
A local health and wellbeing clinic is inviting Milnrow and Newhey residents - and anyone else who fancies a look around - to celebrate the start of a new chapter this weekend.

After 17 years at its Hornby Street clinic, Rainbow Health Group is moving to a brand-new home, and is holding an open day on Saturday 8 August from 11am to 3pm to welcome the community through the doors.

The clinic offers a range of treatments including sports massage, clinical massage, acupuncture, K-Laser therapy, podiatry and rehabilitation, helping people recover from injuries, manage pain and improve their overall wellbeing.

Its new address is Unit 9A, Southgate Industrial Park, Green Lane, Heywood, OL10 1ND.

Visitors on the day can explore the new clinic, meet the team, and learn more about the treatments and services on offer, with complimentary light refreshments provided. There will also be a charity raffle in aid of Help 4 All, and the Mayor and Mayoress will officially open the clinic at 1pm.

"Whether you've been visiting us for years or have never heard of Rainbow Health Group before, everyone is welcome," the clinic said. "We'd love to see you there and celebrate this exciting new chapter with our local community."

articles.title: Milnrow author helping children cope with grief through heartfelt storybooks
articles.excerpt: Milnrow author Jane Somers is helping children understand bereavement and pet loss through two beautifully illustrated storybooks, while donating hundreds of copies to hospitals and hospices.
articles.content_html:
A Milnrow author is helping children navigate some of life's most difficult moments through a pair of beautifully illustrated books exploring bereavement and the loss of much-loved pets.

Jane Somers has written two children's books, *Look For The Robin* and *Over Rainbow Bridge*, with the aim of providing comfort, reassurance and hope for young readers experiencing grief.

Drawing on gentle storytelling and colourful illustrations, Jane's books tackle subjects that many families find difficult to discuss, helping children understand loss in an age-appropriate and compassionate way.

Her first book, *Look For The Robin*, tells the story of a friendly robin who reminds grieving children that the special people they have lost are still watching over them and that they continue to be loved. The book has resonated with families, schools and support organisations, with Jane using proceeds from sales to give something back to the community.

Thanks to the support of readers, she has now donated more than 200 copies of the book to hospitals, hospices and other worthy causes, helping children facing bereavement access the story free of charge. Customers ordering directly from her website also receive a handmade robin clay heart trinket as a keepsake.

Jane's second book, *Over Rainbow Bridge*, focuses on another form of grief that is often underestimated – the loss of a family pet. Written in rhyme and accompanied by warm illustrations, the story follows the bond between children and their beloved animals, reassuring young readers that although their pet has crossed Rainbow Bridge, the love and memories they shared remain forever.

The book aims to help parents start conversations about pet loss in a gentle, positive way, recognising that the death of a much-loved animal is often a child's first experience of bereavement. Every copy purchased through Jane's online store includes a complimentary bookmark.

Child psychologists have long recognised the importance of helping children understand grief through honest but reassuring conversations. Books can provide a safe and accessible way for young readers to explore difficult emotions, ask questions and recognise that feelings such as sadness, confusion and loss are a normal part of bereavement.

Jane says her ambition has always been to create stories that offer comfort while giving families practical tools to support children during challenging times. By combining uplifting messages with beautiful illustrations, she hopes her books provide reassurance that love continues even after someone, or a cherished pet, has gone.

Both books retail at £9.99, excluding postage and packaging, and are available directly through Jane's website. As well as supporting an independent local author, every purchase helps her continue donating copies to hospitals, hospices and organisations supporting bereaved children.

Jane's work is another example of the creativity found within Rochdale borough, using the power of storytelling not only to entertain but to make a genuine difference in the lives of local families and children across the country.
